newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan, Iraq discuss ways to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: Jordan, Iraq discuss ways to boost ties.

text.p: Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali and Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz discussed on Saturday ways of boosting bilateral ties, which include trade under the U.N. oil-for-food sanctions concession to Baghdad.

"Our meeting was cordial and constructive and we discussed bilateral ties between us and follow-up to implementing our (trade) agreements which are proceeding smoothly," Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz told reporters.
Jordan renewed this year a $220 million annual trade agreement under which it barters goods for Iraqi oil.

Amman is keen to improve political ties with Iraq to help it benefit from the U.N. deal which allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and humanitarian supplies, as an exception to sanctions imposed on Baghdad for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Majali was quoted by the state news agency Petra as saying Jordan wanted an end to Iraqi suffering caused by the embargo.

Jordan ranks among the top countries to have secured deals with Baghdad under the scheme, with over $120 million worth of orders obtained so far for products ranging from detergents and soap to medicine.
Aziz, on his way to Baghdad after a visit to China and Moscow, said those two countries supported an end "as soon as possible" to the U.N. sanctions.
"This impression was not just in the two capitals but also in Europe and the Arab world," Aziz said.
